clue.text: Ship's staff welcoming officer's charm

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the pole carrying a vessel's sails

explanation.surface: A ship's crew greeting an officer who carries a good-luck token.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after officer stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good luck, which is what a lucky charm does.

clue.text: Labour leader appears dishevelled in old clothes

indicators.note: something dishevelled is untidy and disordered, so the letters are messed up
the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: The Labour Party leader turns up scruffy, wearing tatty old garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old clothes' reads as a noun phrase, but it is the archaic verb: to apparel someone is to dress them.
explanation.definitionFit: To apparel is an archaic verb meaning to dress or attire, so 'apparels' matches 'clothes' used as a verb.

clue.text: Stared vacantly at Guardian's first barred puzzle

definitions.note: a verb phrase; gazed takes 'at' as well

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: Azed is the Observer's famous barred crossword

explanation.surface: A solver staring blankly at the Guardian's difficult barred-grid crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: A barred puzzle has bars instead of black squares; Azed is the best-known one, set in the Observer, the Guardian's Sunday sister.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze is to look steadily and often absently, so gazed fits staring with an empty, vacant expression.

clue.text: Regime's case against guns

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer shell, the opening and closing letters around the contents

explanation.surface: A regime's legal case opposing firearms ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guns' is not weapons but the verb: to gun an engine is to rev it hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To gun an engine means to accelerate it sharply, the same as revving it up.

clue.text: Hard to see it enabling reforms

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters before take a new form

explanation.surface: Something that enables reform turns out to be hard to perceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Intangible describes what cannot be touched or grasped, so it is difficult to perceive or pin down.

clue.text: Trade union rebelled following regressive measure that's emblematic of old regime

definitions.note: the answer is the emblem itself; 'that's' makes it a thing

indicators.note: coming after, so one word is placed behind the other
regressing means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A union revolting against a backward-looking policy symbolic of a past government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudor rose, red and white combined, was the badge of the Tudor dynasty that ruled England 1485-1603.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-and-white flower badge symbolised the Tudor dynasty, a royal house that ruled England centuries ago.

clue.text: You can't teach this one a lesson!

definitions.text: You can't teach this one a lesson!

parts.words: You can't teach this one a lesson!
parts.note: surface reading: an unruly pupil who refuses to learn
setter's reading: you literally cannot teach a pupil who is absent from class

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like exasperation at a stubborn child; literally, a pupil skipping school is not there to be taught.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a child who stays away from school without permission, so misses every lesson.

clue.text: Red Nose Day cast backed campaign

definitions.note: a verb with its object: backed the campaign

indicators.note: metal that is cast is melted and moulded into a new shape

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: The cast of a Red Nose Day show supported the charity drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Nose Day is a British comedy charity fundraiser. The definition takes in 'campaign' as its object.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give public support or approval, so endorsing a cause is backing it.

clue.text: Dead quietly buried in kind of service held by American church

indicators.note: something buried lies inside the ground, so one piece is put within another
something held is gripped on both sides, so it sits between the letters around it

parts.note: a tea service, a set of cups and pot
piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A quiet burial at a funeral service in an American church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'service' is a funeral, but the letters come from a tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At peace' is a gentle euphemism for having died, resting after death.

clue.text: One of life's little necessities that's free of charge

definitions.text: One of life's little necessities that's free of charge

parts.words: One of life's little necessities that's free of charge
parts.note: surface reading: some small essential thing you don't have to pay for
setter's reading: a tiny particle in every atom, essential to matter, with no electric charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Free of charge' sounds like costing nothing; in physics it means electrically neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle in nuclei carries zero electric charge and is essential to the atoms that make up living things.

clue.text: Become irritated when restaurant includes tip for "hosting"

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the restaurant word surrounds the other
the tip of a word is its very end, here its front letter

explanation.surface: A diner getting annoyed when the restaurant adds a service charge for hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but it picks out the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to feel impatience or annoyance, as at a restriction one dislikes.

clue.text: Urchin blended to a paste with duck

indicators.note: blended ingredients are mixed together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A recipe: mash the sea urchin to a paste with some duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urchin' suggests a street child; here it is the marine animal. 'With' joins the duck's O to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea potato is a burrowing heart urchin, a spiny marine creature found on British beaches.

clue.text: Incendiary material gutted bank

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides taken out, so the middle letters are removed

parts.note: dry stuff used to start a fire

explanation.surface: A bank burned out by arsonists using incendiary material.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the middle two letters, ND, from the six-letter word for fire-starting material.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a row or rank, as of seats or keys, which is what a tier is.

clue.text: They get drunk and spoil gossip about woman

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: People who get drunk and ruin things by gossiping about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' sounds like people, but the things that get drunk are cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaritas are tequila cocktails, things that are drunk, so they 'get drunk' in the passive sense.

clue.text: Poorly men, to me, are what could determine doctor's rate?

indicators.note: something poorly is in bad shape, so the following letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Sick men ask what instrument could tell a doctor their heart rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doctor is a name for a cooling sea breeze, such as the Fremantle Doctor in Western Australia, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemometer is an instrument that measures wind speed, so it could gauge how fast a breeze called the Doctor blows.

clue.text: Popular dictator's going off locking people up

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words aloud for someone to write down

parts.note: milk that is going off is turning sour

explanation.surface: A dictator once popular has turned to imprisoning people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like the tyrant of the surface; it means a person dictating, so the second part is spoken: IN plus TURNING said aloud gives INTERNING.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine people, especially enemy aliens or suspects in wartime, without trial.

clue.text: Concentrate less and hence start late

indicators.note: starting late means missing the opening, so each word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to focus less and therefore begin later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentrate' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a distilled extract; 'and' joins the two shortened words.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract of a plant or flavouring, such as vanilla essence.

clue.text: Special preserve of ancillary officer following revolution

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second piece goes behind the first
a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read the other way

explanation.surface: A support officer's private reserve after a political revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra jam is a UK labelling grade for jam with a higher fruit content than standard jam.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a premium grade of fruit spread, so it is a superior kind of preserve.

clue.text: Choice cut by the three leading establishments in Bow

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: a bow is a curve or bend

indicators.note: the three leading letters are the opening three of the word

explanation.surface: The finest cut of meat sold by the top three butchers in Bow, an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London, but here it is a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: Best end is the prime part of a lamb or veal neck, a choice joint sold by butchers.

clue.text: First person quote on the radio makes sense

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard rather than seen, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: A broadcaster quoting someone in the first person makes sense on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Did very little as American lunged, piercing heart

indicators.note: something piercing goes right into another thing, so it sits inside

parts.note: in American usage the past tense of dive is dove

explanation.surface: Someone stood idle while an American lunged and stabbed a victim in the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' marks the US past tense: Americans say dove where British English says dived.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs slowly while idling, so figuratively the phrase means just keeping going with minimal activity.

clue.text: Bad guy infiltrating government agency reveals bug

indicators.note: an infiltrator gets inside an organisation, so one word goes within the other

explanation.surface: A villain infiltrating a spy agency is exposed as a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: In a spy story a bug is a hidden microphone; here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a large insect known for its loud chirping, and bug is a general word for an insect.

clue.text: Disheartened would-be sire that's not covered dam

indicators.note: losing its heart means the inside goes, so just the outer pair remain
uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, leaving only the inner letters

explanation.surface: A dejected would-be father whose hopes are blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' and 'sire' look like a horse breeder's mother and father; dam is the barrier across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low barrier built across a river to control its flow, a small type of dam.

clue.text: To begin with, Edward Elgar composed to entertain

indicators.note: composing means arranging parts into something new, so the letters are rearranged
what something begins with is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: Edward Elgar, the English composer, wrote music to entertain from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the composer of the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to amuse or delight them with stories or lavish hospitality.

clue.text: Search and interrogate one charged in absentia

indicators.note: in absentia means while not present, so that part is missing from the word

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: Police search for and question a defendant tried in his absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One charged' sounds like the accused in court; it is a charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a long search or pursuit for something, as for the Holy Grail.

clue.text: The most important and original case study in Christian literature

indicators.note: something original is newly made, so the letters take a novel arrangement
in places the word before inside the phrase after

explanation.surface: A seminal case study of Christian writings, both important and original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case study' reads as one academic term but splits into two pieces. Ascendent is a variant spelling of ascendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendant means dominant or in a controlling position, having the greatest power or influence.

clue.text: Home of the indigenous Plains Indians originally

definitions.text: Home of the indigenous Plains Indians originally

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word gives only its starting letter

parts.note: initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A description of the traditional dwelling of Native Americans on the Great Plains.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and its last four words also give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipi is the cone-shaped tent of hides on poles used by Plains peoples such as the Sioux.

clue.text: Consuming hummus in Greek wraps

indicators.note: a wrap encloses its filling, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: Eating hummus inside Greek flatbread wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraps' looks like the flatbread of the surface but signals concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Using up resources means consuming them; both describe expending something.

clue.text: Rather slow article by poet

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, Italian author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A rather slow-moving piece of writing by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: One school friend's admitted relating to religious celebration

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the first pieces go inside the friend word

explanation.surface: A pupil's school friend is allowed into a religious festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on friend stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paschal means relating to Easter or Passover, the major feasts of Christianity and Judaism.
